clues.text: This city lies on the banks of the greatest river in the land, in the southeast of its state. Low bluffs lift it just above the wide water.
clues.narrowing: Points to a city on the Mississippi River in the southeast of its state.

source.quote: The city of Baton Rouge lies on the banks of the Mississippi River in southeastern Louisiana's Florida Parishes region.

clues.text: Winters here are mild and summers are hot and humid, with heavy rain through the year. Damaging winds and tornadoes can strike in any season.
clues.narrowing: Keeps wet, storm-prone Gulf South river cities.

source.quote: It has mild winters, hot and humid summers, moderate to heavy rainfall, and the possibility of damaging winds and tornadoes yearlong.

clues.text: In 1846, state lawmakers picked this river town as the new capital. It took the place of a great port town down the river.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to the city designated in 1846 to replace New Orleans.

source.quote: In 1846, the state legislature designated Baton Rouge as Louisiana's new capital to replace New Orleans.

clues.text: Long ago, explorers found a red pole standing here. It marked the boundary between the hunting grounds of two tribes.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital's name comes from a red boundary pole.

source.quote: The explorers saw a red pole marking the boundary between the Houma and Bayagoula tribal hunting grounds.

clues.text: The governor of Louisiana works in this town by the river. The men and women who make state laws meet in the tall capitol here.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and lawmakers of Louisiana work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital city of the U.S. state of Louisiana

reveal.blurb: French explorers named this river city for the red pole that marked a tribal boundary in 1699. It became the state capital in 1846, and its 34-story capitol is the tallest state capitol in America. The building is the capitol, and the city is the capital. Baton Rouge is the capital of Louisiana.
